newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya's central bank sells floating rate T-Bonds.
newsitem.headline: Kenya's central bank sells floating rate T-Bonds.

text.p: The Central Bank of Kenya held its first public floating-rate Treasury bond auction on Monday, which it dated January 15 1997, bank officials said.
The bank said it accepted 63 bids worth 17.610 million shillings from a total 77 bids valued at 260 million shillings.

The bonds will earn interest at a rate equal to the weighted quarterly moving average of the 91-day treasury bills. At the auction last Thursday, 91-day T-bills fetched an interest rate of 21.575, according to central bank figures.
The highest price per 100 shillings at the bond's auction was 101.50 percent while the lowest was 98.20 percent.

In January, the central bank increased the minimum investment on treasury bills to a million from January 2, 1997 hoping that investors of lesser amounts would invest in the one-year floating rate Treasury bond, whose return is comparable to T-bills.
The floating T-bonds are designed to develop the secondary market and serve smaller investors.
The next auction will be on February 12, 1997.
